mainTopic: Whether a vow linked to an offering attaches to its original forbidden status or to its current status
overview: The גמרא tries to prove that a person who links his vow to an offering is pointing to its original forbidden status, from before the blood was sprinkled. First it brings the משנה's case of 'like נותר, like פיגול', since these only exist after זריקת דמים. רב הונא בריה דרב נתן answers that the משנה may mean נותר of an עולה, which stays forbidden as קרבן. When רבא asks why the משנה didn't just say 'meat of an עולה', the גמרא explains the משנה's 'לא מיבעיא' style: the נותר and פיגול case teaches that the vow is not linked to a Torah prohibition, a דבר האסור. Next the גמרא brings a ברייתא about vowing 'like the day my father died', with שמואל's comment. At first it seems to show that the vow reaches back to the original day despite many permitted days since. The proof falls away once שמואל's real wording is given: he kept the vow every year from that day on. Finally רבינא opens a new proof from the משנה about חלת אהרן and תרומת לחמי תודה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof attempt from נותר and פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that נותר and פיגול only exist after the blood is sprinkled, yet the משנה says a vow linked to them takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: But נותר and פיגול are things that happen after the sprinkling of the blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from the משנה, which says that saying 'like נותר' or 'like פיגול' makes a vow take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the blood of a שלמים is sprinkled, its meat may be eaten, so it is no longer forbidden as קרבן. נותר and פיגול only come into being at that later stage. If the vow still works, it seems the person is reaching back to the offering's original forbidden status.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of an offering left over past the time allowed for eating it
An offering made invalid by a wrong intention about when it would be eaten
Sprinkling the offering's blood on the מזבח, after which the meat may be eaten
But look, isn't it so that...? (opens a proof or challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think נותר and פיגול are forbidden because of a vow. They are forbidden by the Torah. The question is which earlier status of the offering the person is attaching his vow to.

phrases.english: But נותר and פיגול
phrases.notes: This refers back to the משנה's case of someone who says 'like נותר, like פיגול.'

phrases.english: are after the sprinkling of the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא נוֹתָר וּפִיגּוּל לְאַחַר זְרִיקַת דָּמִים הוּא
steps.raayaObject: That a person who links his vow to an offering is linking it to the offering's original forbidden status
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that 'like נותר, like פיגול' makes a vow take effect

steps.title: Maybe it means נותר of an עולה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן rejects the proof: the משנה may be talking about נותר of an עולה, which stays forbidden even after the blood is sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב נתן said to him: It is talking about נותר of an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן pushes back on the proof by giving a different way to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is burned completely and is never eaten, so even after זריקת דמים its meat stays forbidden as קרבן. If the משנה means an עולה, the vow can work by linking to a status that is still in force, so there is no proof about the original status.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח and never eaten

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבא, who answers him in the next line.

phrases.english: It is about notar of a burnt-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן בְּנוֹתָר שֶׁל עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by limiting the משנה to an עולה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely by offering another way to read the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה means an offering that becomes permitted after זריקת דמים, but an עולה never does

steps.title: Then why not just say 'meat of an עולה'?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges: if the משנה means an עולה, it should simply have said 'meat of an עולה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, let it teach 'with the meat of an עולה'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב הונא's reading by asking why the משנה chose such a roundabout way of saying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vow works only because the עולה is forbidden as קרבן, then mentioning נותר or פיגול adds nothing. The simpler wording 'meat of an עולה' would have been enough, so the משנה's wording seems to argue against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a problem that follows from what was just said)
Let it teach (the משנה should have said...)

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
let it teach 'with the meat of a burnt-offering'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אִם כֵּן לִיתְנֵי בִּבְשַׂר עוֹלָה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן's reading that the משנה means נותר of an עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the vow works because of the עולה's קרבן status, the משנה should have used the simpler and clearer wording 'meat of an עולה'

steps.title: The משנה is using a 'not only' style
steps.stepSummary: The answer: plain meat of an עולה is obviously forbidden, so the משנה teaches the less obvious case of נותר and פיגול of an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is saying a 'needless to say' case: needless to say 'meat of an עולה' is forbidden, since he links it to a קרבן. The case of נותר and פיגול of an עולה is the one that needed teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by explaining that the משנה skipped the obvious case on purpose and taught the harder one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Linking a vow to 'meat of an עולה' clearly works, because he is naming a קרבן. The משנה picked נותר and פיגול of an עולה because that case is less obvious, so it is the one worth teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say (the obvious case is assumed, the harder case is taught)
Links his vow to another item, giving it that item's forbidden status
An offering, which is forbidden for personal use
It was needed (to be taught)

phrases.english: It is speaking in the style of 'it is not necessary':
It is not necessary to say that 'meat of a burnt-offering' is forbidden,
since he is linking it to an offering,
notar and piggul of a burnt-offering needed to be taught,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's wording as a 'לא מיבעיא' style
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think that only plain 'meat of an עולה' works for a vow, while 'נותר' or 'פיגול' of an עולה would point to a Torah prohibition, a דבר האסור, so the vow would fail
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה mentions נותר and פיגול of an עולה on purpose, as the harder case that needed teaching

steps.title: Why the נותר and פיגול case teaches something new
steps.stepSummary: Without the משנה, we might think he meant the Torah prohibition of נותר or פיגול, which is a דבר האסור, and that the vow fails. The משנה teaches that it works.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought he meant 'like the prohibition of נותר, like the prohibition of פיגול,' making him like one who links his vow to a דבר האסור, so the item would not become forbidden. The משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by explaining exactly what new thing the נותר and פיגול case teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow can only work by linking to something forbidden through a vow, like a קרבן. Linking to something forbidden by the Torah, a דבר האסור, does not work. We might have thought 'like נותר' points to the Torah prohibition of נותר, but the משנה teaches that he is pointing to the עולה's קרבן status, so the vow takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (the mistaken first thought)
Something forbidden by the Torah itself, which cannot be used to make a vow
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: A vow works only when linked to something forbidden through a vow, like a קרבן, and not to a דבר האסור. Saying 'like נותר of an עולה' counts as linking to the קרבן, so רב הונא's reading holds up.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer saves רב הונא's reading. Because the משנה can be about an עולה, it no longer proves that a vow attaches to an offering's original status.

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say
'like the prohibition of notar, like the prohibition of piggul,'
phrases.notes: He means: we might think the person had in mind the Torah ban on נותר and פיגול, not the offering itself.

phrases.english: and he would be like one who links it to a forbidden thing,
and it would not become forbidden; so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 4 by spelling out the new point
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the mistaken first thought that the משנה comes to remove
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Like נותר or פיגול' refers to a Torah prohibition, a דבר האסור, so the vow would not take effect
steps.terutzMaskana: He is linking his vow to the עולה's קרבן status, so the vow takes effect

steps.title: A ברייתא about vowing 'like the day my father died'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that describes the Torah's איסר vow, along with שמואל's comment that the vow works only if he had vowed on that original day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Which is the איסר vow the Torah mentions? A person said: 'I will not eat meat or drink wine, like the day my father died,' or 'like the day my teacher died,' or 'like the day גדליה בן אחיקם was killed,' or 'like the day I saw ירושלים destroyed.' And שמואל said: this works only if he had a vow on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא with a comment from שמואל. This step sets up the source; the next step draws the proof from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case links today to a special sad day when he did not eat meat or drink wine. שמואל adds that the link works only if that day was forbidden to him through a real vow. The next step asks which day he is really linking to.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow that forbids something to oneself (the Torah's word in במדבר ל)
I hereby (declare)
Bound by a vow
The leader whose murder is remembered on the Fast of גדליה

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Which is the 'prohibition' mentioned in the Torah?
phrases.notes: The Torah uses the word אִיסָּר for a vow in במדבר 30:3.

phrases.english: He said: 'I hereby will not eat meat
and will not drink wine
like the day on which his father died,'
or 'like the day on which his teacher died,'
or 'like the day on which Gedaliah son of Ahikam was killed,'
or 'like the day I saw Jerusalem in its destruction.'
And Shmuel said:
And this is only if he was bound by a vow on that day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה about נותר and פיגול was turned aside, the גמרא brings a new source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a person links his vow only to the current (permitted) state of the thing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא with שמואל's comment seems to show that the vow reaches back to an original forbidden day, even though many permitted days came in between.

steps.title: The proof: he links to the original day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the case as a Sunday when the father died, with many permitted Sundays after it, and concludes that the person links his vow to the original forbidden status.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? Isn't it where today is a Sunday, the day of the week when his father died? Even though there were many permitted Sundays since then, the ברייתא says the food is forbidden. Learn from this that he links his vow to the original status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof from the ברייתא: the vow works by pointing back to the first, forbidden Sunday, not to the permitted Sundays in between.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since then, plenty of Sundays were permitted days. If a person linked his vow to the current state, the vow should fail. The ברייתא says it is forbidden, so he must be pointing to the original vowed day. The same should be true for שלמים after the blood was sprinkled.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
Sunday (the first day of the week)
Permitted status
He links his vow to the original status of the thing

steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof held, it would answer the main question of the sugya: a vow linked to שלמים after the sprinkling would work.

phrases.english: What is the case?
Is it not, for example, where he is standing on a Sunday
the day on which his father died,
and even though there are many
permitted Sundays,
yet it teaches that it is forbidden.
Learn from this that he links his vow to the original status.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? לָאו כְּגוֹן דְּקָאֵי בְּחַד בְּשַׁבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That a person links his vow to the original forbidden status (בעיקר הוא מתפיס).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of 'like the day his father died' together with שמואל's comment that he vowed on that day.

steps.title: שמואל really meant he kept the vow every year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: שמואל actually said the vow works only if he has been under the vow from that day on, so the day is forbidden now too.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל's statement was actually said like this: שמואל said, this is only if he has been bound by a vow from that day onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof by giving the correct wording of שמואל's comment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the corrected version, he vowed every year from the day his father died. So the day he points to is forbidden right now, and he is linking to the current status. The ברייתא no longer proves that he links to the original status.

keyTerms.meaning: This is how it was actually stated
Has been continually bound by a vow
And onward

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions of שמואל. The first version, 'on that day,' supported the proof. The real version, 'from that day onward,' cancels it.

phrases.english: As for Shmuel's statement, it was stated like this:
Shmuel said:
And this is only if he has been continually bound by a vow
from that day onward.
phrases.notes: He means he kept the vow every year on that date. So that day is still forbidden to him now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns aside the proof drawn in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא entirely, without deciding the main question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof depended on the wrong wording of שמואל. In the real wording, the day is forbidden right now, so he links to the current status.

steps.title: רבינא opens a new proof from חלת אהרן
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes the משנה: linking to חלת אהרן or his תרומה leaves the item permitted, which suggests that linking to תרומת לחמי תודה makes it forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Come and hear: 'Like the חלה of אהרן' or 'like his תרומה,' the item stays permitted. This implies that 'like the תרומה of the תודה loaves' makes it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a new source and draws an inference from it. This sets up a new attempt to answer the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלה and תרומה are forbidden by the Torah, not by a person's vow, so linking to them does nothing. The משנה's wording implies that the תרומה of the תודה loaves, which comes from קדשים, does work in a vow. The גמרא will next connect this to the question of the original status versus the current status.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to the כהן
The portion of produce given to the כהן
The loaves brought with a קרבן תודה
Permitted

phrases.english: Ravina said: Come and hear:
'Like the challah of Aaron,' or 'like his teruma': it is permitted.
This implies: 'like the teruma of the thanks-offering loaves': it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the ברייתא was rejected, רבינא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: The main question of whether a person links his vow to the original status or to the current status.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (נדרים 13b) about חלת אהרן and his תרומה, and the inference about תרומת לחמי תודה.
